newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says peace at crossroads because of Israel.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says peace at crossroads because of Israel.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Thursday Middle East peace was at a difficult crossroads and Israeli policies were encouraging violence.
He appealed to Palestinians to keep faith that peace was possible and to Israelis to realise the best guarantee of security was to recognise the rights of others.

"We now stand at a difficult crossroads because the peace process faces a serious trial which could threaten its ability to continue after it made great grogress," Mubarak told the nation in a recorded address on state television.

"I fear the violence in the occupied territories might escalate to the limits of repression because of the continuing (Israeli) policy of building settlements, trying to impose a fait accompli, anticipating the results of negotiation and violating Arab and Moslem rights in East Jersualem," he added.
Mubarak was speaking on the 15th anniversary of the last stage of Israeli withdrawal from the Sinai peninsula under the Israeli-Egyptian peace treaty signed in 1979.

"If the reasons for the violence are not addressed objectively and earnestly, then the situation heralds dire consequences, because no one, however strong, can tame an angry people who feel their rights have been violated," he said.
"We appeal to the Palestinian people to rise above feelings of frustration and despair and keep faith that a just peace will prevail despite all difficulties.

"We also call on the Israeli people to understand that nothing is equal to the value of peace and that coexistence, good neighbourliness and accepting the rights of others are the guarantees of real security in relations between peoples," President Mubarak added.
